title: VideoML standard pipeline (browser): playback component, bundle builders, brand.video slot
description:
## Goal
The browser half of the VideoML capability in `@anthusai/papyrus`: the `article-video` playback component, video-mode/script helpers, the preview and browser bundle builders, and a `brand.video` slot through which a publication supplies its own scene components (title slide, quote card, rhythm tokens, pictogram art). TI's brand-specific components stay in the TI repo.

## Context (verified)
- Papyrus `develop` already has `components/article-video.tsx` (`ArticleVideoFigure`, themed MP4 via `resolveThemedVideoSrc` from `lib/themed-image.ts`) and `lib/graphql-content-repository.ts` `normalizeVideoAsset` (L796+) / `parseVideoRoles` that read `MediaAsset` rows of `type: "video"`. It does NOT have `lib/video-mode.ts` and `lib/video-script.ts` (they exist in the TI fork: `lib/video-mode.ts` 1.6 KB, `lib/video-script.ts` 1.7 KB with `parseVideoScriptRef`, `videomlItemSlug`, `normalizeDevPreviewDsl`), `scripts/videoml/{build-browser-bundle.mjs, build-preview-bundle.mjs, capture-scene-preview.mjs, export-seed-video-scripts.mjs}` (Papyrus has only `build-browser-bundle.mjs`, entry `publications/threat_intelligence/videoml/browser-bundle.tsx` L91), or `public/videoml/ti-preview.html`.
- TI main (sha 90582117355e3ff724d1abef554454d64bf6b432) files for reference: `components/article-video.tsx` (9 KB, newer than Papyrus's), `lib/video-mode.ts`, `lib/video-script.ts`, `publications/threat_intelligence/videoml/{browser-bundle.tsx, preview-bundle.tsx (22 KB), preview-stage-fit.ts, preview-timing.ts, pictogram-video.tsx, ti-title-slide.tsx (12.5 KB), ti-quote-card.tsx, ti-video-rhythm.ts, Videos.stories.tsx}`, `scripts/videoml/*`, `public/videoml/ti-preview.html`, test `publications/threat_intelligence/tests/test-video-script.cjs`.
- `package.json` has script `videoml:bundle` = `node scripts/videoml/build-browser-bundle.mjs`; `@videoml/toolchain` / `@videoml/cli` 1.0.0 are on npm (see `PPY-085f79`). `PPY-672ea6` adds `SiteBrand.components` and `demoEdition` slots in `lib/site-brand.ts`; this ticket adds `video`.

## Exact changes
1. `lib/site-brand.ts` `SiteBrand`: `video?: { bundleEntry: string; sceneComponents?: Record<string, string>; rhythm?: Record<string, unknown> }` where `bundleEntry` is a path relative to the publication root of a TSX module that registers the brand's scene components (`@videoml` custom elements) and is bundled with the generic ones; Papyrus ships the generic components (`title-slide`, `quote-card` generic versions) and the bundle builders; the brand's TI-style variants live in the TI repo.
2. Generic modules into Papyrus (copy from TI main, then genericize; no `ti-` names): `lib/video-mode.ts`, `lib/video-script.ts` (rename `normalizeDevPreviewDsl` replace pair into a brand-provided `elementAliases` map: `{ "quote-card": "ti-quote-card" }` comes from `brand.video.sceneComponents`), `components/article-video.tsx` (take TI main's newer version if it is a superset; keep the public props `video`, `slug`, `figureClassName`), `renderers/pretext/*` call sites unchanged.
3. Bundle builders: `scripts/videoml/build-browser-bundle.mjs` and `build-preview-bundle.mjs` read `brand.video.bundleEntry` from the publication's `papyrus.config.ts` (resolve through `lib/define-site.ts`; esbuild is already used; output `public/videoml/browser-bundle.js` and `preview-bundle.js`); no TI path remains (`publications/threat_intelligence/videoml/browser-bundle.tsx` L91 goes). Ship them in the package (`packages/papyrus/scripts/stage.mjs` copies `scripts/videoml/*`) and expose a bin `papyrus-app videoml-bundle` (`packages/papyrus/bin/papyrus-app.mjs` + `src/`), so a publication runs `npx papyrus-app videoml-bundle` instead of copying scripts.
4. Papyrus's own repo keeps TI's components only through its dev config: `papyrus.config.ts` (repo root, from `PPY-672ea6`) sets `brands: [..., threatIntelligenceBrand]` where `threatIntelligenceBrand.video = { bundleEntry: "publications/threat_intelligence/videoml/browser-bundle.tsx" }`; these files are NOT in the package (the stage check from `PPY-672ea6` forbids `publications/`).
5. Docs: add to `docs/video-pipeline.md` (from `PPY-085f79`) the "Brand video components" section: how a publication registers `brand.video`, how to build bundles, how the Python `VideoConfig.browserBundle` points at the output.

## Data shapes
```ts
// publication papyrus.config.ts
brand: { ..., video: { bundleEntry: "publication/video/browser-bundle.tsx", sceneComponents: { "quote-card": "acme-quote-card" } } }
```
`parseVideoScriptRef(item)` returns `{ slug, dsl, targetKind }` from `item.editorial.videoScript` exactly as in TI main.

## Tests
- TS unit: port `publications/threat_intelligence/tests/test-video-script.cjs` to `scripts/test-video-script.ts` (tsx, npm script `test:video-script`): ref parsing, `videomlItemSlug`, alias normalization via a passed-in map.
- Bundle smoke `scripts/test-videoml-bundle.mjs`: with a tiny fixture `bundleEntry` (`scripts/fixtures/video-bundle-entry.tsx`) the builder writes a non-empty `browser-bundle.js` and fails with a clear message when `brand.video` is missing.
- Package check: `node scripts/test-package-contents.mjs` (from `PPY-672ea6`) also asserts `scripts/videoml/build-browser-bundle.mjs` is in the tarball and `publications/` is not.
- Gherkin (cucumber): none needed unless an article page with a video is reachable in demo mode; add `features/article-video.feature` ("An article with a lead video shows a video player with a poster") ONLY if the demo edition already has a video asset; otherwise skip and rely on the component being unchanged.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, existing `test:renderer-config`.

## Acceptance checks
- `npx tsx scripts/test-video-script.ts`, `node scripts/test-videoml-bundle.mjs`, `npx tsc --noEmit` pass.
- In Papyrus's repo with `PAPYRUS_SITE_BRAND=threat-intelligence`: `npm run videoml:bundle` produces `public/videoml/browser-bundle.js` (same as before this change, modulo naming); in a scratch consumer using the tarball: `npx papyrus-app videoml-bundle` builds the bundle from the consumer's own entry.
- `rg -n "ti-" components lib scripts/videoml` shows no TI element names outside `publications/`.

## Dependencies
Blocked by `PPY-672ea6` (brand slots, package-content check), `PPY-78e818`. Pairs with `PPY-085f79` (Python config points at the bundle path) but can run in parallel. Same-file conflicts: `lib/site-brand.ts` (also `PPY-672ea6`: land after it), `packages/papyrus/scripts/stage.mjs` (`PPY-672ea6`, `PPY-39f928`).

## Risks
- TI's `preview-bundle.tsx` (22 KB) mixes generic preview mechanics with TI visuals; the split is a judgment call per component (default: generic mechanics up, visuals stay) and is the main effort driver.
- Bundle builders need `esbuild` and the brand's TSX to resolve React from the consumer's `node_modules`; check alias handling in a scratch consumer.
- The TI repo (Phase 3) will have to delete its copies once this lands; coordinate through the Phase 3 ticket, not here.

## Needs Ryan
Nothing.

## Common rules (apply to every Phase 2 ticket)
- Work from a clean worktree of `origin/develop` (`git -C /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus fetch origin && git worktree add ../Papyrus-worktrees/<this-ticket> -b feature/PPY-961956-<slug> origin/develop`). Never commit to `develop` or `main`; open a PR into `develop`; never merge to `main`. Conventional-commit messages. Update this ticket with branch, PR link and the verification output.
- `AGENTS.md` rules that bind this work: no backward-compatibility shims or fallbacks (clean breaks); backend tooling in Python unless noted; Pretext owns text measurement (do not measure DOM in React); read `AGENTS.local.md` before ANY AWS/Amplify/sandbox command; never run `ampx pipeline-deploy` locally (sandbox only).
- Note on language direction: Ryan's 2026-10-05 correction (epic comment 4174c5) says Papyrus is being ported from Python to TypeScript. Phase 2 follows the approved design in docs/standard-site.md (Python CLI/Lambdas + `papyrus-newsroom`). Keep new Python logic in small pure functions with fixture-driven tests so it can be ported; do not add new Python dependencies beyond those named here.
- Tests: Python unit tests are `unittest` under `procedures/newsroom/tests/` (run: `poetry run python -m unittest procedures.newsroom.tests.<module> -v`); backend Gherkin is `behave` under `features_backend/` with steps in `features_backend/steps/` (run: `poetry run behave features_backend/<file>.feature`); UI Gherkin is cucumber-js + Playwright under `features/` (run against a dev server: `npm run dev` then `PAPYRUS_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3001 npx cucumber-js features/<file>.feature`); TypeScript unit tests are `scripts/test-*.ts` run with `npx tsx` (add an npm script `test:<name>` in package.json).
- Install: `poetry install --extras "newsroom markus"` and `npm ci`. Verify `markus --version` prints 0.5.1 (PyPI `anthus-markus` 0.5.1 emits IR `schema_version: 1`).

comments.text: ADDED SCOPE (Ryan, 2026-10-06): this ticket must include a REAL end-to-end render proof of the whole VideoML pipeline (PPY-085f79 Python side, merged in #118, + this ticket's browser bundle): take one scratch article (short, ~20-30 s of narration), build its script from a CMS item (FakeAuthoringClient or a local item; NO real backend), build the browser bundle from a scratch publication's brand.video entry, run  with the real @videoml/cli and the real OpenAI TTS (OPENAI_API_KEY is available in the environment; never print or log it, never commit it; cap the narration to ~30 s so cost is cents), then verify the MP4 with ffprobe (duration, streams, resolution), and check it plays: reference it from a MediaAsset and load the article page in the dev server with the player. Also record what 'vml pipeline' needs in a scratch publication (undeclared gsap/framer-motion/d3/three deps), as input for an upstream VideoML fix. Keep the output MP4 out of git (attach it to the ticket comment path or the scratchpad); delete scratch dirs when done.

comments.text: PR https://github.com/AnthusAI/Papyrus/pull/120 (branch feature/PPY-961956-videoml-browser), CI python/ts/smoke green. Built: SiteBrand.video slot, lib/video-mode.ts, lib/video-script.ts (alias map), ArticleVideoFigure preview mode, standard entry + browser/preview bundle builders reading brand.video.bundleEntry, papyrus-app videoml-bundle [--preview], docs section, tests. REAL RENDER: scratch publication (tarball contents + real @videoml/cli 1.0.0 + OpenAI TTS gpt-4o-mini-tts alloy, 229 chars, well under 1 cent) produced a 16.37 s MP4: h264 1280x720 30fps + aac mono 24 kHz, 458584 bytes, at scratchpad/evidence/scratch-field-notes.mp4. Verified in the Papyrus dev server (demo outputs): MP4 mode plays (videoWidth 1280, duration 16.37, readyState 4) and preview-iframe mode renders and advances. UPSTREAM VIDEOML GAPS: @videoml/cli fails at 'vml --help' on missing gsap, then framer-motion, d3, three (one at a time); playwright undeclared (render fails 'Playwright is required' after TTS has already been paid); @videoml/player undeclared for browser preview; bundling @videoml/toolchain/renderer needs p5, lottie-web, animejs marked external (undeclared dynamic imports); the standard browser bundle (window.Babulus, window.renderFrame) is not shipped in npm, so each publication must supply it; published toolchain package.json says version 0.0.0-semantic-release and cli depends on that placeholder; React 18 UMD loaded from unpkg at render time.
